lesson.sourceStem: An RN is delegating tasks to a licensed practical nurse (LPN) and an unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP). Which task is appropriate to delegate to the UAP?

sources.title: NCSBN: National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation

initial.question_stem: A trained UAP may collect routine vital signs under facility policy but is not authorized to administer medications. Which task may the RN delegate?

options.label: A
options.text: Obtain scheduled vital signs on a stable patient

options.label: D
options.text: Teach a patient how to inject insulin

initial.key_cue: The patient is stable and the task is authorized.
initial.why_correct_short: Routine measurement fits this UAP’s stated training. The RN follows up on findings.

rationales.B: New symptoms require nursing assessment and judgment.
rationales.C: Medication administration is outside this UAP’s stated authorization.

initial.one_line_fix: Check patient stability, task requirements, demonstrated competence, and local policy.

retry.question_stem: A trained UAP can record routine intake and output under facility policy. Which task may the RN delegate for a stable patient?

options.label: A
options.text: Decide whether low urine output indicates dehydration

options.label: C
options.text: Evaluate whether the fluid plan is working

retry.key_cue: The task is routine measurement for a stable patient.
retry.why_correct_short: Recording the amount fits the stated role; interpreting it remains with the nurse.

rationales.A: Interpreting the cause requires nursing judgment.
rationales.B: Teaching the plan requires nursing judgment.

retry.one_line_fix: Distinguish collecting a measurement from interpreting its meaning.
